title: unified-rollouts-add-e2e-tests-and-stability-guards-for-shadow-canary-autorollback
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: several recent rollouts revealed flakiness in our automated rollback paths when shadow and canary traffic overlap under load. This PR adds an integration test harness for unified rollouts (canary / A/B / shadow) and introduces small runtime guards to make metric-driven auto-rollback more deterministic.

What this PR does: - Adds end-to-end integration tests that simulate concurrent shadow and canary traffic with synthetic latency/error profiles. Tests validate metric matching, rollback triggers, and graceful fallback. - Introduces a per-rollout deduper for metric windows to avoid double-counting shadow and canary events when a single request is duplicated across routes. This avoids spurious threshold breaches. - Extends the rollout controller to emit clearer audit events for each automated rollback decision (reason, metric snapshot, snapshot_id). - Adds CI job rollout-integration that runs the new e2e tests in the perf-canary matrix (nightly + on PR when labels include "unified-rollouts"). - Adds a small backoff window before auto-rollback when transient spikes are detected (configurable by rollout policy).

Checklist: - [x] implementation and unit tests - [x] integration/e2e tests - [x] perf smoke runs locally - [x] docs: rollout-controller audit events described (redwood-docs) - [x] linked Linear tickets updated

Related: Linear ENG-4210 (stability for shadow canary autorollback), ENG-4302 (e2e rollout test coverage).

review_comments: Alex Chen (review): Can you clarify how the deduper identifies duplicated events across shadow/canary? Looks like it keys on request_id + window; please add a comment and test for clock skew scenarios.
Sofia Martinez (author): Added comments and a new test that simulates 250ms clock skew. The deduper now tolerates skew up to configured window (default 1s).
Dana Kline (review): CI job looks good, but nightly perf runs are expensive. Please gate heavy profiles behind a feature flag in the pipeline so we can opt-in while stabilizing.
Sofia Martinez (author): CPI change made; heavy profiles run only when ROLLOUT_HEAVY=1 in pipeline. Updated docs section to mention opt-in.
Priya Natarajan (approval): Verified e2e locally against a dev cluster and confirmed no regression on A/B weighted rollouts. Approving.
release_notes: Add e2e integration tests and stability guards for unified rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow). Adds metric deduper to prevent double-counting and a configurable backoff window before auto-rollbacks. New CI job: rollout-integration.
